x-bump-note:
1.5.0 -> 1.6.0 (plan pln-deferrals-carry-both-sides-and-7d1c7e, docs/plans/2026-08-06-deferrals-carry-both-sides.md) declares the optional `case_against` string on a task row, made REQUIRED by an allOf conditional on the two scope-cut dispositions (`backlogged`/`wont_do`) — the same trigger set as the sibling `pm_approved` conditional, deliberately excluding `spun_off` for the identical reason it does (nothing leaves the corpus, so there is no scope cut to argue against; re-widening that set would re-open a boundary the PM ruled on 2026-08-05). Requested by claude-klabauter-em (cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-06-claude-klabauter-em-deferrals-need-both-sides-not-a-ratify-list.md), whose point is that a deferral surfaced to the PM as an ID list is close to unactionable: the row carried only `disposition_detail`, the case FOR cutting, and an EM proposing a cut has by construction already convinced itself — the argument that could change the PM's mind had nowhere to live. Classified nested-field-additive: a new optional property on an existing entity object, made conditionally required only on dispositions that are themselves scope decisions. Every row valid under 1.5.0 that carries no closed disposition remains valid; existing `backlogged`/`wont_do` rows across the ~84 already-stamped plans are NOT retro-fitted (the plan's Out-of-scope names this explicitly) and are tolerated by the presence-only, non-hard-failing posture every conditional in this file shares. Hard rejection of a missing or blank `case_against` is claude-klabauter-resident and landed 2026-08-06 as claude-klabauter `eee18fb77`, in `schema_validate.py`'s `_cf_plan_tasks_disposition_shape` — the plan-tasks-specific caller, NOT the shared `_cf_disposition_shape` this comment previously named. That shared validator is also handoff `carried_items`' validator, which has no `case_against` field at all, and its docstring carries a negative-spec against disposition-token-specific logic; a gate there would have imposed a plan-tasks-only requirement on every handoff claude-klabauter validates. It is the enforcement leg asked of that repo in the plan's C8 memo, alongside the revendor of this bump.

1.4.0 -> 1.5.0 (task-spine-dependency-declaration) declares the optional `depends_on` array on a task row — an array of {chunk, gate_kind, note?} objects giving the two NON-computed authoring/execution gates (`output-consumption-runtime`, `epistemic-premise`) a declarable home on the spine. Requested by example-market-data-repo-em (cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-06-example-market-data-repo-em-plan-tasks-schema-has-no-depends-on.md), which correctly identified that docs/wiki/writing-plans.md § Substrate-Migration Sequencing step 2 instructed authors to write `depends_on` while this schema defined no such property — an author could follow the wiki or the schema, not both. The sender's proposed bare `array of string` was WIDENED to an array of objects carrying `gate_kind`: skills/execute-plan/SKILL.md Phase 1.6 requires every imposed gate to name its kind, and a bare chunk-id list forces the EM to re-derive the kind from prose at execute time — the same re-derivation defect the discriminator exists to eliminate, one level down. Classified nested-field-additive: a new optional field on an existing entity object (schema-version-gate.md § bump classes), narrowing no declared domain and invalidating no existing row. Fleet-wide grep across example-doctrine-repo, claude-klabauter, example-cockpit-repo, example-retrieval-repo, example-retrieval-repo-ue-addon, example-market-data-repo and example-game-workbench-repo found ZERO existing emitters of `depends_on` inside any plan `## Tasks` block, so there is no back-compat constraint in either direction. docs/wiki/writing-plans.md step 2 was amended in the same change to prescribe exactly this shape — the two must move together or the contradiction simply reverses direction.
title: plan-tasks
description:
Per-row schema for the plan `## Tasks` task-spine YAML block (one task object per row). Full authoring contract, parser-locate rule, malformed-row disposition, and harvest routing: docs/wiki/writing-plans.md § Machine-Parseable Task Spine and docs/wiki/canonical-artifact-shapes.md § Addressable-Section Convention.

Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-07-09-plan-full-coverage-and-deferred-harvest.md § C1 (pinned task-spine contract).

id.description: Chunk id (e.g. C1, D1). Unique within the plan. Deferred rows conventionally use the D<n> prefix, but the prefix is a convention, not a schema-enforced discriminator — `deferred: true` is the actual signal.

title.description: One-line brief. Becomes the queue-entry title on harvest (coordinator-queue-append --schema improvement-queue, or the lessons-outbox title on the doctrine-edit/snippet-sync-update path).

change_kind.description: WIDER UNIVERSAL change-kind enum. SSOT: docs/wiki/lessons-outbox-schema.md § Change-kind enum (do NOT duplicate the enum values elsewhere — point there instead). Harvest routing: the project-tier subset (script-edit, skill-edit, wiki-append, wiki-new, hook-edit, agent-prompt-edit, doc-edit, test-edit, code-edit, config-edit, verification) routes to coordinator-queue-append --schema improvement-queue; doctrine-edit and snippet-sync-update route to coordinator-lesson-promote (lessons-outbox) instead — the improvement-queue schema rejects those two kinds at project scope. These values name the SURFACE changed, not the flavour of the change — do not coin a work-shape token (a bash-to-Python port of a bin/ utility is script-edit); an unrecognized value routes nowhere on harvest.

surface.description: Harvest/coverage PRIMARY-TARGET field — a single path or subsystem. Maps to the queue entry's `surface` field ONLY. See docs/wiki/writing-plans.md § Machine-Parseable Task Spine for the surface-vs-write-files-set distinction.

queue_scope.description: Which improvement-queue the harvest writes into. Default 'project' writes to the plan's own repo-local state/improvement-queue/. 'central' is a per-deferral opt-in that maps to `coordinator-queue-append --queue-scope central`.

deferred.description: true => this row is NOT shipped by this plan; it is a harvest candidate for coordinator-harvest-deferrals. false (default) => the row is shipped in-plan and is not a harvest target.

pm_approved.description: Required when deferred is true (cross-field rule — see the allOf conditional below). Records that the PM ratified the scope cut. false or absent on a deferred:true row is a plan-coverage-checker flag. Only deferred:true AND pm_approved:true rows are harvest candidates; a deferred row with pm_approved:false or absent is NOT harvested. READ-TOLERATED, not authoritative, on any plan carrying a plan-document-level `grouping_approvals` block (a GOVERNED plan — see plan.schema.json, where that field is defined): on a governed plan this bare bool is NOT the authorization signal for a closed row: authorization lives in the plan-document `grouping_approvals` block, keyed by the grouping (`do`/`defer`/`ruled_out`) the row's `disposition` derives into (see schema_validate.py's `check_plan_tasks_grouping_approval`). On a LEGACY plan (no such block present anywhere in its frontmatter), this field is unchanged from its original role — the sole authorization signal for a deferred/closed row, read-tolerated exactly as before this distinction existed.

body.description: Optional multi-line detail block. Maps to the queue entry's `body` field on harvest.

disposition.description: Row resolution state. 'open' (default) => not yet resolved. 'coded' => shipped in a specific commit (disposition_ref is a single hex SHA). 'spun_off' => moved to a new plan (disposition_ref is a single repo-relative path). 'backlogged' => deferred to the improvement/debt backlog (disposition_ref is a single repo-relative path). 'wont_do' => explicitly declined (disposition_ref forbidden; disposition_detail required). Mirrors the shape of `carried_items[].disposition` (D1). Cross-field enforcement matrix: D2/D3/D4 in the originating plan; hard rejection happens in schema_validate.py (C2), not here — see the allOf $comments below for what this schema itself does and does not hard-fail.

disposition_ref.description: Forward pointer/evidence for a non-open disposition — semantics depend on `disposition` (SHA for coded, repo-relative path for spun_off/backlogged, forbidden for wont_do). Separate from `disposition_detail`, which carries rationale prose (D2).

depends_on.description: OPTIONAL declared sequencing edges into this row, one entry per predecessor. ABSENT (or empty) means no non-write-overlap gate — it does NOT mean the row is unconditionally parallel, because write-overlap gates are computed elsewhere and are never written here. Exists so the two gate kinds that are NOT derivable from the file-write graph have a home on the spine instead of living only in wave-map prose the EM must re-derive at execute time. Authoring procedure: docs/wiki/writing-plans.md § Substrate-Migration Sequencing step 2. Gate-kind semantics and the malformed-serialization rule: skills/execute-plan/SKILL.md Phase 1.6 § gate-kind discriminator. NEGATIVE SPEC — three of the six discriminator gate kinds are deliberately unwritable here, see `gate_kind`'s enum note.

chunk.description: The predecessor row's `id` (e.g. C1, D2) within THIS plan's spine. Singular referent — one predecessor per entry; a row with three predecessors carries three entries, which is why this field is an array member rather than the singular `depends_on: <Task K>` scalar the wiki originally prescribed.

gate_kind.description: Which Phase 1.6 gate this edge is. DELIBERATELY RESTRICTED to the two gate kinds that a mechanical wave-builder cannot derive on its own. `output-consumption-runtime`: the predecessor's artifact must EXIST AT RUNTIME when this row executes (the layout/substrate case — a directory, schema, or persistence path the producer opens). `epistemic-premise`: the predecessor decides whether this row should exist at all, so there is no interface to pin and nothing to author against until its verdict lands. NEGATIVE SPEC, three exclusions, each for its own reason: (1) `file-write-overlap` is COMPUTED by the wave-builder from the chunks' write targets (skills/execute-plan/SKILL.md:128) and must NEVER be hand-declared here — a hand-written write-overlap edge is a second, silently-desyncing source of truth for a fact the graph already knows. (2) `output-consumption-content` and (3) `contract-change` do not gate AUTHORING at all: Phase 1.6 requires both to downgrade to concurrent-with-pinned-interface with verification deferred to merge, so declaring either as a dependency edge is precisely the malformed serialization the discriminator exists to catch — pin the interface in the consumer's body instead. `none` is likewise unwritable: absence of the field is how a row says it has no declared gate.

note.description: OPTIONAL one-line rationale for the edge — what specifically must exist (or be decided) before this row runs. Reader-facing prose; no consumer parses it. Cheap and worth writing: the edge's KIND is machine-readable via `gate_kind`, but the reason a human should trust the edge is not.

disposition_detail.description: Rationale/detail prose for a CLOSED disposition (spun_off/backlogged/wont_do — D2/D4). Required for wont_do (in place of disposition_ref) and for spun_off/backlogged alongside their disposition_ref. NOT required for coded: per D3, coded is evidence of work done, not a scope decision, so it carries no PM rationale to record — see the allOf conditionals below for the exact per-disposition requirement.

case_against.description: The strongest HONEST case for doing this work now, plus the EM's recommendation, confidence, and what would change it. Required when disposition is backlogged or wont_do (D4-adjacent, mirroring pm_approved's trigger set — see the allOf conditional below); deliberately NOT required for spun_off (nothing leaves the corpus, so there is no scope cut to argue against — see the pm_approved conditional's own $comment for the ruling this mirrors). Presence-only / NON-hard-failing at this schema layer, exactly like the sibling conditionals: this only checks that the key exists on the row, not that its prose is non-vacuous. A strawman satisfies this schema while defeating the rule it exists to serve — the field asks for the strongest honest case, not a token counter-argument to grep past.

allOf.$comment: Cross-field rule: pm_approved is required-when-deferred. JSON Schema if/then encodes this — when deferred is true, pm_approved MUST be present (and, per the field's semantics, true) for the row to be a valid harvest candidate. A deferred:true row with pm_approved absent or false remains structurally valid JSON (this schema does not hard-fail it — see the malformed-row-disposition note in the top-level description) but is flagged by plan-coverage-checker, the enforcement surface for this cross-field rule.

then.$comment: Presence, not truthiness — this only checks that pm_approved is a key on the row. A deferred:true row with pm_approved:false still validates here (schema does not hard-fail it); the truthiness check (pm_approved must equal literal true) is flagged by plan-coverage-checker, not schema-rejected.

allOf.$comment: Cross-field rule: disposition: coded requires disposition_ref matching a single hex SHA (7-40 hex chars) — DR-096's singular-referent constraint (D2): no ranges, comma-lists, or branch names.
Cross-field rule: disposition: spun_off requires disposition_ref as a single repo-relative path (DR-096 singular-referent — one path, not a list).
Cross-field rule: disposition: backlogged requires disposition_ref as a single repo-relative path (DR-096 singular-referent — one path, not a list).
Cross-field rule: disposition: wont_do requires disposition_detail and FORBIDS disposition_ref (there is no forward pointer for a declined row).

Cross-field rule: the two SCOPE-CUT dispositions (backlogged/wont_do) require pm_approved (D4, as narrowed by DR-2026-08-05 below). `coded` is deliberately NOT gated: per D3 it is evidence of work done, not a scope decision, so it needs no PM authorization. `spun_off` is NOT gated either, as of 2026-08-05: D4 originally widened the trigger to all three closed dispositions, but spun_off moves work to another plan rather than dropping it — nothing leaves the corpus, so there is no scope cut for the PM to ratify. backlogged and wont_do DO drop work, and choosing between them is a PM judgment the EM does not self-issue; claude-klabauter-em's 2026-08-05 ask to relax all three to a recorded-reason gate was declined for exactly these two (see cross-repo/outbox for the reply). Do not re-widen this enum to include spun_off, and do not narrow it further, without a PM ruling. Presence-only / NON-hard-failing at this schema layer, exactly like the deferred=>pm_approved rule's own $comment above: this only checks that pm_approved is a key on the row, not that it equals literal true. Hard rejection of `pm_approved is not True` on a closed disposition is schema_validate.py's job (C2's _cf_plan_tasks_disposition_shape — the plan-tasks-specific caller, not the shared _cf_disposition_shape), not this file's. LEGACY-ONLY BRANCH: on a GOVERNED plan (one whose frontmatter carries a plan-document-level `grouping_approvals` block — see plan.schema.json), claude-klabauter's frontmatter layer derives a governed schema variant at validation time (`schema_validate.py`'s `_plan_tasks_schema_without_pm_approved_required`) that STRIPS this exact branch — any `allOf` branch whose `then.required` names `pm_approved` is removed from the derived copy — because a governed plan's closed-row authorization is instead checked against the row's grouping approval state (`check_plan_tasks_grouping_approval`), not this per-row bool. This branch therefore governs LEGACY plans only; do not hand-copy a second, governed-only variant of it into this file. The derivation is computed once, at runtime, from this single branch — a hand-maintained duplicate here would be a second home for the same rule, free to silently desync from the branch it duplicates.

Cross-field rule: the two SCOPE-CUT dispositions (backlogged/wont_do) also require case_against — the both-sides ask (cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-06-claude-klabauter-em-deferrals-need-both-sides-not-a-ratify-list.md; docs/plans/2026-08-06-deferrals-carry-both-sides.md). Mirrors the pm_approved conditional immediately above with the SAME trigger set, deliberately: `spun_off` is excluded for the identical reason pm_approved excludes it — nothing leaves the corpus, so there is no scope cut to argue against, and re-widening this trigger set to include spun_off would silently re-open a boundary the PM already ruled on 2026-08-05. Presence-only / NON-hard-failing at this schema layer, exactly like every other conditional in this file: this checks that case_against is a key on the row, not that its prose is non-vacuous. Hard rejection is claude-klabauter-resident and landed 2026-08-06 (`eee18fb77`) as absent/empty/whitespace-only refusal — presence and non-blankness only. Anti-strawman detection was deliberately NOT built: a case against phrased weakly enough to lose satisfies any mechanical check, so that is a doctrine and review-gate problem (docs/wiki/plan-coverage-checker.md Lens 2b specificity sub-check), not a validator's. NOT-SUPPRESSED-ON-GOVERNED: the mirroring stops at the trigger set. Claude-klabauter's governed-plan schema variant (`_plan_tasks_schema_without_pm_approved_required`) strips only allOf branches whose `then.required` names `pm_approved`; this branch requires `case_against`, so it survives, and claude-klabauter's own gate fires regardless of governed=True. That is correct and deliberate on both sides — `case_against` is the argument FOR the cut, not the authorization OF it, so it is orthogonal to the governance model. Do not read the `mirrors the pm_approved conditional` line above as implying governed plans suppress this one.

Cross-field rule: the CLOSED dispositions other than wont_do (spun_off/backlogged) also require disposition_detail — rationale prose alongside the evidence pointer (D2/D4: 'the verbatim PM reasoning ... goes in disposition_detail — which is already required on every CLOSED disposition'). wont_do's disposition_detail requirement is already covered by its own conditional above. `coded` is deliberately excluded here: per D3 it is evidence of work done, not a scope decision, and is therefore NOT a CLOSED disposition — close_out_and_stamp's auto-resolution to coded writes only disposition + disposition_ref (the commit SHA) and must remain schema-valid with no detail.
